minutes.headline: School Committee will not rebuild its budget for a possible override — it will send finance a memo of priorities instead
minutes.summary: The committee spent most of the meeting on the unresolved FY26 budget/override standoff with the finance committee, deciding to send a memo of what would be restored (not a full line-item budget) if an override passes, and discussed spending options for roughly $500,000 in free cash. It also approved a slate of four superintendent finalists, approved a co-op ski team funding plan, closed out old class-fund accounts, and tabled a decision on opening school-choice seats to the next meeting.

attendees.name_as_heard: the secretary for the athletic department

public_comment.topic: Asked whether there were meeting notes on the ski team item since it was on the agenda.
Praised the committee's superintendent screening work and urged members to set aside disagreements going into finalist interviews.
Thanked the superintendent for publicly explaining the math behind the level-services and town-manager budgets.

budget_items.what_was_said: Warrants from March 17 to March 26, 2025 were presented totaling this amount, with no line item transfers reported this cycle.
The remaining balances in these two closed class accounts were identified for transfer into a new donations line.
After more than two years of no contact with the class, the account was closed and its balance moved to the donations line.

budget_items.topic: Middle school vs. high school athletic fee
budget_items.what_was_said: The athletic secretary explained the participation-count discrepancy for softball was due to middle schoolers paying one fee tier and high schoolers another.

budget_items.topic: Ski team program cost and per-student fee
budget_items.what_was_said: The AD reported this year's total ski program cost and per-athlete cost, and discussed billing co-op member schools per student after subtracting the current or a possible new athletic fee.
A member cited the program's enrollment and low net cost to argue for keeping it and expanding similar offerings.

budget_items.topic: Primary School air conditioning grant (phase two)
budget_items.what_was_said: A state grant and utility incentive would cover most of the second phase of mini-split installation, leaving a town share that must be secured through the FY27 capital plan by September 2027.

budget_items.topic: Primary School AC project, capital plan listing
budget_items.what_was_said: The 10-year capital plan currently lists the pre-grant project cost; with the grant applied the town's share would be much smaller.

Members discussed that school choice students bring a cherry-sheet payment of roughly this amount per student and also affect the district's Chapter 70 census, though the added Chapter 70 amount itself was not quantified at the meeting.
The superintendent presented three categories for using free cash -- restoring positions, restoring expense cuts, and one-time investments -- to be weighed against this amount available.
The position was budgeted at a level the town manager fears will not attract qualified applicants; free cash could be used to raise the salary line.
The committee discussed leasing or buying vans to cut bus costs for athletic transport but held off pending research into federal safety rules and what neighboring districts use.
A member totaled the proposed free-cash-funded position restorations against a much smaller bus cost figure, questioning the priority order.
Food services will again sell pre-bagged lunches during town meeting at this price, contingent on the food-and-drink vote.

budget_items.topic: Warrant article to supplement FY26 school operating budget
budget_items.what_was_said: One warrant article reviewed would supplement the FY26 school operating budget by this amount; no vote was taken on it this meeting.
The chair reported no funding source exists for this article and that the town was not including it on the warrant, recommending the committee pass over it.

transfers.description: Remaining class of 2003 and class of 2010 funds moved into a new donations line within the student activity account
Remaining class of 2007 funds moved into the donations line within the student activity account

decisions.decision: School choice proposals (10 seats at grade 9, and possibly seats at other grade levels) will come back for a vote at the next meeting rather than tonight.
The chair will reach out directly to the finance committee chair to try to reach agreement on the budget/override memo before the next meeting.
Superintendent search interviews will be consolidated into as few days as possible, likely including a Saturday after town meeting, rather than four separate weeknights.
Any proposed athletic summer camp will have an early registration deadline so an under-enrolled camp can be cancelled with about a month's notice to families.
The school committee goals item was deferred; members will review the document on their own and raise items later.
The committee will pass over the track and field capital article since the town is not putting it on the warrant and no funding source exists.

what_happened.line: The committee voted to send finance a memo of budget priorities, not a rebuilt line-item budget, ahead of a possible override.
It accepted a slate of four superintendent finalist candidates recommended by its screening committee.
A vote on opening additional school-choice seats was pushed to the next meeting.
The superintendent outlined three uses for free cash -- restoring positions, restoring expense cuts, or one-time purchases -- with no choice made among them.
The committee approved a co-op ski team plan splitting program costs among member schools' athletes.

why_it_matters: The finance-committee memo, not a finished budget, is what will describe what gets restored if voters approve an override at town meeting.
A school-choice vote, once taken, affects both a per-student payment to the district and the district's Chapter 70 state aid count.
The free-cash discussion touches whether cut positions -- including a finance-office role the town manager says is underpaid -- get restored before FY26 begins.
